prerequisites: Basic physics knowledge from school education

learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully completed this module will have fundamental physical knowledge that they will need in advanced modules of electrical engineering.

Based on the treatment of energy, power and efficiency as well as cyclic processes and heat engines, students can describe the sustainability of technical processes (e.g. for mobility and heat generation).

Students who have successfully completed this module can exchange ideas with students/graduates of other engineering disciplines about fundamental physical principles common to all engineering disciplines.

syllabus_topics: Mechanics: Kinematics and dynamics of translation and rotation, law of conservation of energy, power, efficiency, physical quantities and units, SI system, measurements
Thermodynamics: Temperature, main laws, heat capacity, heat conduction, ideal gases, cyclic processes (Carnot process), heat engines
Oscillations and waves: Undamped, damped and forced oscillations, waves, superposition of waves, wave properties of light
assessment_rules: The choice between a written exam and a portfolio exam is up to the respective lecturer. The portfolio exam comprises a total of 100 points, consisting of three written tests. In the first two tests, a maximum of 33 points each can be achieved, and in the third test, 34 points can be achieved. Experimental work involves approximately 5 experiments, each lasting 90 minutes. For the written exam, refer to the valid study regulations.
